jurisdiction: Fulton County (Fulton County Schools and Atlanta Public Schools)
number: Educational Special Purpose Local Option Sales and Use Tax (ESPLOST)
official_title: Shall the special one percent sales and use tax for educational purposes currently imposed in Fulton County be reimposed on July 1 2027 upon the expiration of the currently imposed tax, for not longer than 20 consecutive calendar quarters, to raise not more than $2,095,680,577.00 to be used for the following educational purposes: For the Fulton County School District: (A) for acquiring, reconfiguring and developing land for, constructing and equipping, new and replacement schools and support facilities; (B) adding to, upgrading, reconfiguring, renovating, replacing, modifying and equipping existing and replacement schools, support facilities and athletic facilities; (C) making technology improvements and safety and security improvements for schools and facilities; and (D) replacing, purchasing, upgrading or supplementing capital equipment as needed, including without limitation furniture, multi-year textbooks, instructional resources, physical educational equipment, band and music equipment, audio visual equipment, equipment that supports learning and similar equipment; and (E) acquiring and equipping school buses, school police vehicles, support vehicles, transportation vehicles and other capital equipment; in an amount not to exceed $1,306,195,350.00 for the Fulton County School District, all as more fully described in the Notice of Election. For the Atlanta Independent School System: (A) for acquiring, reconfiguring and developing land for, constructing and equipping, new and replacement schools and support facilities; (B) adding to, upgrading, reconfiguring, renovating, replacing, modifying and equipping existing and replacement schools, support facilities and athletic facilities; (C) making technology improvements and safety and security improvements for schools and facilities; (D) replacing, purchasing, upgrading or supplementing capital equipment as needed, including without limitation furniture, multi-year textbooks, instructional resources, physical educational equipment, band and music equipment, audio visual equipment, equipment that supports learning and similar equipment; and (E) acquiring and equipping school buses, school police vehicles, support vehicles, transportation vehicles and other capital equipment; at a total maximum cost of $789,485,227.00, for the Atlanta Independent School System as more fully described in the Notice of Election. If the imposition of the tax is approved by the majority of the qualified voters residing in Fulton County, such vote shall also constitute approval of the issuance of general obligation debt of the Atlanta Independent School System in the principal amount of up to $350,000,000.00 payable from its portion of the tax for the purpose of funding all or a portion of the APS Projects located in Fulton County.
plain_summary: Keeps Fulton County's 1-cent school sales tax going for up to five more years from July 1, 2027, at the same rate. It can raise up to about $2.1 billion: up to $1.31 billion for Fulton County Schools and $789 million for Atlanta Public Schools (APS), for school buildings, technology, security and buses. A yes also lets APS borrow up to $350 million, repaid from its share of the tax.
yes_means: Fulton's 1-cent school sales tax continues from July 1, 2027 for up to five years, and APS may borrow up to $350 million against its share.
no_means: The current 1-cent school sales tax ends when it runs out (APS says June 2027), and APS and Fulton County Schools would need other money for building projects.
current_law: Fulton already collects this 1-cent tax under the cycle voters approved in 2021. For APS, that cycle has raised $650.8 million so far and ends in June 2027 (APS staff briefing, as summarized by the Center for Civic Innovation). Sales-tax money like this can only go to buildings, equipment, technology and buses, not salaries.
fiscal_impact: Ballot caps: $2,095,680,577 total; $1,306,195,350 for Fulton County Schools; $789,485,227 for APS; up to $350,000,000 in APS general obligation bonds, paid from APS's share of the tax. APS staff forecast roughly $831 million for APS over the five-year cycle and are budgeting for 90% of that; $831 million is what APS's Fulton cap plus its $41.5 million DeKalb cap add up to.
pass_threshold: Simple majority of Fulton County voters
confusing_wording_note: "Reimposed" means continued: the 1-cent tax is already collected, so a yes keeps your sales tax where it is. The $350 million APS borrowing is not a separate question; a yes on the tax approves it too, and the ballot says it's repaid from APS's share of the tax. The vote is countywide, so Atlanta voters also help decide Fulton County Schools' share (most of APS's money comes from this question, not DeKalb's). Atlanta voters who live in DeKalb don't see this question; they vote on DeKalb's E-SPLOST instead.

supporters_case.text: Fulton County Schools, whose board voted unanimously to ask voters for the extension, says the tax is a pay-as-you-go way to fund its capital plan with no interest costs, and that it spreads the cost across everyone who shops in Fulton instead of relying on bonds or a higher property tax rate.

opponents_case.text: We found no organized campaign or official argument on this side.

jurisdiction: DeKalb County (DeKalb County Schools, Atlanta Public Schools and City Schools of Decatur)
official_title: Shall the special one percent sales and use tax for educational purposes currently imposed in DeKalb County be reimposed on July 1, 2027, upon the expiration of the such currently imposed tax, for not longer than 20 consecutive calendar quarters, to raise not more than $1,046,154,324.00 to be used for the following educational purposes: For the DeKalb County School District: (A) adding to, upgrading, reconfiguring, renovating, replacing, modifying and equipping existing and replacement schools, support facilities, athletic fields and physical education facilities; (B) for acquiring and developing land for, constructing and equipping, new and replacement schools and support facilities, as well as additions to existing facilities. (C) for installing capital improvements for various existing and new schools, buildings and facilities (D) for providing hardware, software, and related infrastructure and making technology improvements; and (E) replacing, purchasing, upgrading school buses, support vehicles, and other capital equipment. in an amount not to exceed $946,773,776.00 for the DeKalb County School District, all as more fully described in the Notice of Election. If imposition of the tax is approved by a majority of the voters within the DeKalb County School District, such vote shall also constitute approval of the issuance of general obligation debt of the DeKalb County School District in the principal amount of not to exceed $500,000,000 for the purpose of funding a portion of the above projects of the DeKalb County School District. For the Atlanta Independent School System: (A) for acquiring, reconfiguring and developing land for, constructing and equipping, new and replacement schools and support facilities; (B) replacing, updating, renovating, adding to, modifying, and equipping certain critical systems, infrastructure, safety systems and non-critical if and as needed, based on the condition and identified deficiencies; (C) adding to, upgrading, reconfiguring, renovating, replacing, modifying and equipping existing and replacement schools, playgrounds, support facilities and athletic facilities as needed; (D) making technology improvements and safety and security improvements for schools and facilities; (E) replacing, purchasing, upgrading or supplementing capital equipment as needed, including without limitation furniture, multi-year textbooks, instructional resources, physical educational equipment, kitchen equipment, band and music equipment and equipment that supports learning; and (F) acquiring and equipping school buses, school police vehicles, support vehicles, transportation vehicles and other capital equipment; at a total maximum cost of $41,504,193.00, for the Atlanta Independent School System as more fully described in the Notice of Election. For the City of Decatur School System: (A) for the acquisition, construction, renovation, modification, addition, repair, replacement, demolition of, improvement and equipping of existing and new school buildings and other facilities, including other buildings and greenspace useful or desirable in connection therewith; (B) to acquire and install safety and technology improvements throughout the school system, including computers, systems, sensors, and related hardware and infrastructure; (C) to acquire school buses, school-related vehicles, and transportation equipment, including infrastructure for electric vehicles; (D) for school and facilities improvement, energy conservation, and maintenance projects; (E) to acquire supplemental capital equipment for the school system, including any property, real and personal, useful and desirable in connection with the projects listed in the Notice of Election; and (F) To pay the cost of acquiring certain assets that are being leased or subject to installment purchase by the City Schools of Decatur and to retire all or a portion of any outstanding general obligation debt of the City of Decatur incurred on behalf of the City Schools of Decatur for school projects in an amount not to exceed $57,876,355.00 for the City Schools of Decatur, all as more fully described in the Notice of Election.
plain_summary: Keeps DeKalb County's 1-cent school sales tax going from July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2032, at the same rate. It can raise up to about $1.05 billion: up to $947 million for DeKalb County Schools, $41.5 million for Atlanta Public Schools and $57.9 million for City Schools of Decatur, for school buildings, technology and buses. It also approves up to $500 million in DeKalb County School District borrowing to start projects sooner.
yes_means: DeKalb's 1-cent school sales tax continues from July 2027 to June 2032, with up to $41.5 million for APS, and DeKalb's school district may borrow up to $500 million.
no_means: The current tax (E-SPLOST VI) ends June 30, 2027 or when it hits its cap, and the three school systems would need other money for building projects.
current_law: DeKalb voters approved E-SPLOST VI with 81% of the vote in November 2021; it runs through June 30, 2027 or until it reaches its cap. DeKalb voters have approved all six earlier E-SPLOSTs. The money can only pay for buildings, equipment, technology and buses, not salaries or benefits.
fiscal_impact: Ballot caps: $1,046,154,324 total; $946,773,776 for DeKalb County Schools; $41,504,193 for APS; $57,876,355 for City Schools of Decatur; up to $500,000,000 in DeKalb County School District general obligation bonds. The district says issuing the bonds would take another school board vote after the referendum.
confusing_wording_note: "Reimposed" means continued, not a new tax. One yes/no covers two things: the sales tax and up to $500 million in DeKalb County School District borrowing. For the borrowing, the ballot counts only voters inside the DeKalb County School District, which doesn't cover most of Atlanta's DeKalb side (APS serves it). So Atlanta voters there help decide the tax and APS's $41.5 million share, not the DeKalb district's bonds. The DeKalb schools handout's "$946.8M" is only DeKalb schools' share; the ballot's total cap is $1.05 billion. Atlanta voters in Fulton don't see this question.

jurisdiction: Fulton County outside the City of Atlanta
number: Transportation Special Purpose Local Option Sales and Use Tax (TSPLOST)
official_title: Shall an additional 0.75 percent sales and use tax be imposed in that part of Fulton County, Georgia, outside of the City of Atlanta, for a period not to exceed five years for the purpose of transportation improvements and congestion reduction.
plain_summary: Renews the 0.75-cent transportation sales tax that Fulton's cities outside Atlanta have used since 2017, for up to five more years. Each city picks and manages its own road and traffic projects. City of Atlanta voters do not vote on this.
yes_means: The 0.75-cent transportation sales tax continues in Fulton County outside Atlanta for up to five years.
no_means: Fulton outside Atlanta stops collecting this 0.75-cent tax when the current one runs out, and the cities lose that money for transportation projects.
current_law: First approved by voters in November 2016 and collected since 2017; renewed by North and South Fulton voters in 2021. Projects are chosen by each Fulton city and managed locally.
pass_threshold: Simple majority of voters in Fulton County outside the City of Atlanta
confusing_wording_note: The ballot says "additional," but this is a renewal: Fulton County says it "would maintain the current rate of 0.75 cents." It is not on City of Atlanta ballots, even though many people outside the city have Atlanta mailing addresses.

supporters_case.text: Fulton County says TSPLOST projects "have improved safety, reduced congestion, and enhanced quality of life" and "have been delivered on time and within budget."

opponents_case.text: We found no organized campaign or official argument on this side.
